'''Mahamadou Diarra''' (born 18 May 1981) is a Malian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]]. He served as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] for the [[Mali national football team|Mali national team]].

==Club career==
===OFI Crete===
Diarra started his professional career at Greek club [[OFI Crete F.C.|OFI]] at the age of 17, being signed after recommendation of his elder brother [[Harouna Diarra|Harouna]], who had joined the club a year earlier.<ref>https://menshouse.gr/bala/46620/pektes-pou-agorastikan-gia-psichoula-ki-apodichthikan-chrysafi (greek)</ref> After a single season at Greece and being watched by clubs such as [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]], he decided to join Dutch club [[SBV Vitesse|Vitesse]].<ref name="kentudezenog">{{cite web|url=https://www.kentudezenog.nl/mahamadou-diarra-1981/|title = Mahamadou Diarra (1981)|date = 21 October 2018}}</ref>

===Vitesse===
Diarra made his debut for Vitesse on 13 August 1999. During his tenure at the club, his playing style was compared to [[Ruud Gullit]] and attracted interest from [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], then coached by [[Carlo Ancelotti]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11923/2200931/no-diarra-contact-say-vitesse|title = No Diarra Contact Say Vitesse}}</ref> During the summer of 2002, after receiving offers from many European clubs, Vitesse sold Diarra to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] by €4 million, although the player favoured a move to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] to rejoin his old manager [[Ronald Koeman]].<ref name="kentudezenog"/> Diarra played a total of 69 league matches and scored nine times for the [[Arnhem]]-based club.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20190121233111/https://pt.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=292344.html]</ref>

===Lyon===
At Lyon, Diarra was a starter in each of his four seasons, playing alongside [[Michael Essien]] and [[Juninho Pernambucano]] in the midfield and helping his side to win the [[Ligue 1]] in each of those seasons.

===Real Madrid===
After [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] head coach [[Fabio Capello]] asked club president [[Ramón Calderón]] to sign "three players", "Diarra, Diarra and Diarra",<ref name="talentspotter.fourfourtwo.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/lassana-diarra-talentspotter|title=Lassana Diarra: Talentspotter|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=1 February 2006|access-date=23 March 2017}}</ref> Real Madrid joined [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the race to sign the midfielder.<ref name=Fulham>{{cite news| url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17177742 | work=BBC Sport | title=Mahamadou Diarra to join Fulham until end of the season | date=27 February 2012}}</ref> Lyon said that Diarra could not leave and put a €40&nbsp;million price tag on him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccerlens.com/where-will-diarra-go-lyon-manchester-united-or-real-madrid/297/|title=Where Will Diarra Go? Lyon, Manchester United, or Real Madrid? - Soccerlens|date=13 July 2006|access-date=20 September 2016|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052337/http://soccerlens.com/where-will-diarra-go-lyon-manchester-united-or-real-madrid/297/|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, on 18 August 2006, Real Madrid agreed a fee of €26&nbsp;million<ref>{{cite web|url=https://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas/2006/08/18/ult59u103801.jhtm|title = Real Madrid acerta a contratação de Diarra, do Lyon - 18/08/2006 - UOL Esporte - Futebol}}</ref> and four days later, Diarra was unveiled at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] by Calderón and was assigned the number 6 shirt.

During the [[2006–07 Real Madrid C.F. season|2006–07 season]], Diarra was a staple in Capello's two-defensive midfielder system. He appeared in 33 out of 38 [[La Liga]] matches, scoring on three occasions. On 18 June 2007, with Real Madrid needing to win against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] to win the [[La Liga|Liga]] for the first time since [[2002–03 La Liga|2003]], Diarra scored an 81st-minute header to give Madrid a 2–1 lead. In the 84th minute, [[José Antonio Reyes]] scored a third goal to ensure Real Madrid were champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730196845/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_3-1_Mallorca.htm |title=Real Madrid C.F. - Official Web Site - Real Madrid 3-1 Mallorca |date=6 December 2013 |access-date=20 September 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206095337/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730196845/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_3-1_Mallorca.htm |archive-date=6 December 2013}}</ref>

Diarra played a pivotal role in the [[2007–08 Real Madrid C.F. season|2007–08]] title defence under new head coach [[Bernd Schuster]], and he established himself as the first-choice [[defensive midfielder]], causing teammate [[Fernando Gago]] to play higher upfield. Real Madrid comfortably won the [[2007–08 La Liga|Liga]], finishing eight points clear of second-placed [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]]. Diarra had now been a league champion for six consecutive seasons, after winning Ligue 1 with Lyon between [[2002–03 Ligue 1|2002–03]] and [[2005–06 Ligue 1|2005–06]], and La Liga with Real Madrid in 2006–07 and 2007–08.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-my/news/3956/transfer-zone/2012/02/27/2932769/fulham-sign-former-real-madrid-midfielder-mahamadou-diarra|title=Fulham sign former Real Madrid midfielder Mahamadou Diarra subject to visa - Goal.com|date=27 February 2012|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref>

[[File:Celebration4 (4199911534).jpg|Diarra (left) with Real Madrid|thumb]]

In October 2008, while playing an international fixture for [[Mali national football team|Mali]] against [[Chad national football team|Chad]], Diarra was stretchered off the field after receiving a blow to his knee. He was rested for a month and made his next appearance in late November, but was forced to undergo surgery after aggravating his knee injury, which ruled him out for the remainder of the [[2008–09 Real Madrid C.F. season|2008–09 season]]. In his absence, Real Madrid signed [[Lassana Diarra]] from [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] as a replacement defensive midfielder, who was issued Diarra's number 6 shirt.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7787323.stm | work=BBC News | title=Real Madrid unveil new boy Diarra | date=22 December 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gfdb.com/Player.3458.Lassana-Diarra.aspx|title=Lassana Diarra|access-date=23 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103095349/http://www.gfdb.com/Player.3458.Lassana-Diarra.aspx|archive-date=3 January 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> After recovering from injury, Diarra only started 8 further matches in two seasons for Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/11673/mahamadou-diarra?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120719214318/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/11673/mahamadou-diarra?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 July 2012|title=Mahamadou Diarra Player Profile - ESPN FC|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> In January 2011, it was reported that Diarra would be leaving Real Madrid, and was linked to several clubs including [[Málaga CF|Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/01/26/2323807/mahamadou-diarra-set-to-leave-real-madrid-for-malaga-report|title=Mahamadou Diarra set to leave Real Madrid for Malaga - report - Goal.com|date=26 January 2011|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref>

===Monaco===

Diarra returned to [[French football league system|French football]] after signing with [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] on 27 January 2011.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/monaco-signs-mahamadou-diarra-from-real-madrid-1.1018598?ref=rss | work=CBC News | title=Monaco signs Mahamadou Diarra from Real Madrid | date=27 January 2011}}</ref> He made his debut in a 0–0 draw against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11819_6712337,00.html | work=Sky Sports | title=Ligue 1 round-up | date=30 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-europe-france-diarra-idUKLDE70Q2OS20110127|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224030056/http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-europe-france-diarra-idUKLDE70Q2OS20110127|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 December 2016|title=Monaco agrees deal to sign midfielder Mahamadou Diarra from Real Madrid|date=27 January 2011|agency=[[The Canadian Press]]|access-date=27 January 2011}}</ref> Diarra left Monaco after the club was relegated to [[Ligue 2]] at the end of the [[2010–11 Ligue 1|2010–11 season]]. After his departure, he remained without a club for the first half of the 2011–12 season and was linked with moves to the Middle East<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insidefutbol.com/2011/09/24/mahamadou-diarra-offered-lucrative-middle-east-option/49649/|title=Mahamadou Diarra Offered Lucrative Middle East Option|date=24 September 2011|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> and English [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/d/doncaster/9606623.stm | work=BBC News | title=Doncaster eye Diarra & Piquionne | date=5 October 2011}}</ref>

===Fulham===
Diarra signed for [[Premier League]] side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on 26 February 2012.<ref name=Fulham/> He agreed to a contract for the remainder of the [[2011–12 Fulham F.C. season|2011–12 season]], with an option for the [[2012–13 Fulham F.C. season|2012–13 season]].<ref name=Fulham/> He made his Fulham debut as a substitute against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 4 March, assisting the fifth goal in a 5–0 win. On 17 March, he made his first start for Fulham in a 3–0 home loss to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/fulham/team-news/team-news-diarra-handed-first-start_20251.html|title=Team News: Diarra handed first start|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Fulham against Bolton Wanderers on 7 April 2012.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17570919 |title=Bolton 0 - 3 Fulham |publisher=BBC
|date=7 April 2012 |access-date=7 April 2012}}</ref>

After impressing manager [[Martin Jol]] throughout his 11 Premier League match, on 17 May, Diarra signed a new one-year contract at the club, keeping him at [[Craven Cottage]] until the end of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/may/17/diarra-extension-confirmed | title = Diarra Extension Confirmed | publisher = Fulham FC | access-date = 17 May 2012}}</ref>

Diarra was one of 12 players released by Fulham at the end of the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2013-14/jun/summer-transfers-2013-ins-and-outs.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630015532/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2013-14/jun/summer-transfers-2013-ins-and-outs.html |archive-date=30 June 2016 |title=Summer transfer window: Ins and Outs |publisher=Premier League |access-date=7 June 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite his release, Martin Jol remained positive on Diarra and vowed to help him over the summer to continue his rehabilitation.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jol: Diarra Staying Positive|url=https://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2013/may/04/jol-diarra-staying-positive|publisher=Fulham Official Website|date=4 May 2013|access-date=20 April 2014}}</ref>

Diarra re-signed for Fulham on 26 March 2014 on a contract that expired at the end of the [[2013–14 Fulham F.C. season|2013–14 season]] in an ultimately unsuccessful attempt to help the club survive relegation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Diarra Rejoins Fulham|url=https://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2014/march/26/diarra-rejoins-fulham|publisher=Fulham FC|access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref>

=== Later career ===

Diarra trained with Championship side [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] throughout the [[2016–17 Brentford F.C. season|2016–17 season]] and made an appearance for the club's [[Brentford F.C. Reserves and Academy#Brentford B|B team]] on 20 September 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/mahamadou-diarra-training-brentford-head-11862104|title=Former Real Madrid and Lyon star training with Brentford|last=Moore|first=Tom|date=9 September 2016|access-date=20 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.brentfordfc.co.uk//news/article/2016-17/brentford-v-leyton-orient-friendly-match-report-3318509.aspx?site=desktop|title=Brentford v Leyton Orient friendly match report|last=FC|first=Brentford|access-date=20 September 2016|archive-date=24 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224030142/http://www.brentfordfc.co.uk//news/article/2016-17/brentford-v-leyton-orient-friendly-match-report-3318509.aspx?site=desktop|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/how-former-real-madrid-star-12781255|title=Former Real Madrid star has become an important man at Brentford|last=Moore|first=Tom|date=23 March 2017|work=getwestlondon|access-date=23 March 2017}}</ref>

==Style of play==
''[[FourFourTwo]]'' magazine described Diarra's playing style with the following forwards in 2006: "Diarra provides aggression, tactical awareness, toughness and the discipline that other players simply lack."<ref name="talentspotter.fourfourtwo.com"/>

==Personal life==
Diarra is a practising Muslim. He observes fasting during the Islamic month of [[Ramadan]],<ref name="goal">{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2009/08/22/1454134/ramadan-fasting-for-real-madrid-trio-lassana-benzema-and|title=Ramadan Fasting For Real Madrid Trio Lassana, Benzema and Diarra|publisher= Dadyal Online |date=22 August 2009|access-date=31 December 2012}}</ref> he maintains that "every coach has respected my decision".<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite news |last=Din|first=Tusdiq|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/596/exclusive/2009/08/24/1456626/exclusive-i-can-keep-fasting-in-ramadan-even-when-i-am|title=Exclusive: I Can Keep Fasting In Ramadan Even When I Am Playing – Fredi Kanoute|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=24 August 2009|access-date=1 January 2013}}</ref>
